newsitem.title: CROATIA: Voting in March 1997 will include Serb enclave.
newsitem.headline: Voting in March 1997 will include Serb enclave.

text.p: The next local elections in Croatia will take place in March and will include the country's last enclave still under Serb control for the first time in five years, state radio said on Monday.
"We concluded they (the elections) will be held on March 16," said Ivica Kostovic, deputy Prime Minister in charge of the reintegration of Serb-held Eastern Slavonia.
Kostovic spoke after a meeting between President Franjo Tudjman and Jacques Klein, head of the U.N. Transitional Administration in Eastern Slavonia (UNTAES).
Klein would ultimately regulate voting in the enclave. Voting elsewhere in Croatia would follow standard procedure.
UNTAES, Croatian and local Serb authorites have completed a census to determine how many people in the enclave are eligible to vote, the radio said.
An estimated 120,000 Serbs now live in Eastern Slavonia. About half are refugees from other formerly Serb-held areas in Croatia.

Kostovic said the talks focused on preparing a document in which Croatia would put a comprehensive offer to the local Serb population, "including all their rights within the Croatian legal and constitutional order".
The agreement would be signed by Klein and the Croatian government although Kostovic did not say when that would happen.
Croatia's Serbian minority rebelled against Zagreb's rule after the country proclaimed independence from federal Yugoslavia in 1991.
The rebel Serbs captured one third of Croatia, including Eastern Slavonia, but Zagreb siezed back all other enclaves in lightning offensives last year.
UNTAES, with 5,000 combat-trained peace troops, took charge of Eastern Slavonia last January with a mandate to gradually restore Croatian government rule in the region by mid-1997.
